title: Truly Pre-Routing Timing Prediction via Considering Power Delivery Network
problem: Pre-routing timing prediction in chip design ignores power delivery network (PDN) effects, leading to inaccurate timing predictions. Existing ML-assisted methods fail to capture IR drop and routing congestion impacts on timing.
motivation: Fast and accurate timing prediction is critical in chip design flow; overlooking PDN effects makes existing methods impractical for real-world circuits.
method: Proposes two specialized encoders—an IR drop-aware encoder and routing congestion-aware encoder—that fuse multimodal data (netlist, layout, PDN) through Pareto optimization to balance utilization across modalities for improved timing prediction accuracy on TSMC 16nm designs.
key_novelty: Pareto optimization-based multimodal fusion that balances IR drop, routing congestion, and netlisting encoders to capture PDN effects in pre-routing timing.
contributions: IR drop-aware and routing congestion-aware encoder pair for capturing PDN effects
Pareto optimization approach for balanced multimodal fusion
Evaluation on large-scale open-source designs at 16nm technology node
Demonstrated superiority over state-of-the-art pre-routing timing methods

metrics.accuracy: improved over SOTA pre-routing timing methods

primary_theme: ML-assisted pre-routing timing with power delivery network awareness
